we generalize Denef's method of deriving and studying first-order equations describing extremal multicenter solutions in 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity to include non-supersymmetric cases and we explicitly solve the equations of this method for the stu model, which is a non-supersymmetric case.

we have found a generalization of Denef’s method to non-supersymmetric multicenter black holes in 4D N = 2 supergravity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the superpotential approach can be extended to non-supersymmetric extremality.

we have generalized the Denef’s method to allow non-superymmetric solutions, and we have found that the solutions to the first-order equations can be expressed in terms of the solutions to the second order equations, and the solutions to the latter can be found by solving a set of algebraic equations.
we can find all non-supersymmetric extremals in the stu model by the superpotential method.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a large class of theories, non-supersymmetric extremality can be achieved by turning on a non-trivial superpotential, which is a function of the scalars only, while the vector fields are set to zero.
the first-order equations describing the multicenter solutions can be obtained in a straightforward way by using the superpotential approach.
, in the presence of non-supersymmetric centers, the superpotential method is still applicable, but the first-order equations become non-holomorphic and the solutions are no longer BPS states.
